_meta.notes: Interview bank for grill-me. types[].cues detect the project type from the request. A question with an empty types list is universal. weight 1-3 is how much the answer changes the build. if_skipped is written as a statement and becomes an assumption when the question is not asked or not answered.

questions.q: What happened that made you want this now?
questions.changes: Sets the real goal, so the build solves the trigger and not just the wording of the request.
questions.if_skipped: The request is a first attempt at a recurring need, and the stated goal is the whole goal.

questions.q: Three weeks from now, what would you be able to point at to say this worked?
questions.changes: Turns success into something observable, which becomes the acceptance test.
questions.if_skipped: Success means the person who asked can use the result unaided on first try.

questions.q: Who will actually use or read this, and how much do they already know?
questions.changes: Sets vocabulary, depth and how much hand-holding the result needs.
questions.if_skipped: The audience is the requester plus one non-expert colleague.

questions.q: What have you tried before for this, and why did it not work?
questions.changes: Avoids rebuilding the thing that already failed and exposes the hidden requirement behind the failure.
questions.if_skipped: Nothing suitable was tried before, so no earlier failure is being repeated.

questions.q: What must this never do or say, even by accident?
questions.changes: Creates hard prohibitions that the acceptance check tests directly.
questions.if_skipped: Nothing beyond the obvious: no invented facts, no private data exposed, no off-brand claims.

questions.q: What would make you send it back and ask for a redo?
questions.changes: Names the reject conditions before the work starts instead of after.
questions.if_skipped: It would be sent back if it is wrong on facts, hard to read, or ignores a stated must-have.

questions.q: Who has to approve this before it counts as done, and what do they care about?
questions.changes: Adds a second reader with their own criteria, which changes tone, proof and format.
questions.if_skipped: The requester is the only approver.

questions.q: Name one example of this kind of thing you love and one you hate.
questions.changes: Gives a concrete taste anchor that adjectives cannot.
questions.if_skipped: No taste reference exists, so a plain, neutral, professional style is used.

questions.q: What happens the day after this ships: who touches it, and does it change over time?
questions.changes: Decides whether to build for handover, editing and upkeep or for one-time use.
questions.if_skipped: It is used once and not maintained, so no upkeep tooling is built.

questions.q: When do you need it, and is that date fixed or a wish?
questions.changes: Sets how much polish and how many options fit inside the time.
questions.if_skipped: There is no hard deadline, and the first version should be complete but plain.

questions.q: What real material can you give me: examples, data, past versions, files, links?
questions.changes: Real input replaces invention, which is the largest source of errors.
questions.if_skipped: No source material exists, so placeholder content is clearly marked as placeholder.

questions.q: What is explicitly not part of this, even if it seems related?
questions.changes: Draws the boundary that stops scope creep and wasted work.
questions.if_skipped: Anything not named in the must-have list is out of scope.

questions.q: What format or tool must the final result arrive in?
questions.changes: Fixes the output format, which limits every design choice after it.
questions.if_skipped: The result is delivered as a file in the most common format for this kind of work.

questions.q: Any hard limits I should know: budget, tools you must use, brand rules, things you cannot install?
questions.changes: Rules out approaches that would be impossible or forbidden in the user's setting.
questions.if_skipped: No special limits apply beyond free, widely available tools.

questions.q: What is the one thing a visitor should do before leaving the page?
questions.changes: Picks the single call to action that the whole layout is built around.
questions.if_skipped: The one action is contacting the owner, and every section leads to it.

questions.q: Where does the visitor come from and what do they already believe about you?
questions.changes: Decides the opening message: cold introduction versus continuing a conversation.
questions.if_skipped: Visitors arrive cold from search or a shared link and know nothing yet.

questions.q: How many pages or sections, and which ones are certain?
questions.changes: Sets site structure and navigation, single scroll or multi-page.
questions.if_skipped: One scrolling page with hero, proof, offer and contact.

questions.q: Is the text written, or should I write it, and do you have real proof (quotes, numbers, logos)?
options: I write it from your notes
I write it, no proof yet
questions.changes: Decides whether copy is a placeholder or the substance of the job, and whether proof blocks exist.
questions.if_skipped: I write the text from the notes given, and proof sections are left out rather than invented.

questions.q: Send two sites whose look you admire and one that feels wrong.
questions.changes: Anchors palette, type, density and mood better than any adjective.
questions.if_skipped: A clean, light, editorial look with generous white space and one accent color.

questions.q: Do you already have a domain and hosting, or a builder like Shopify or Squarespace you must stay on?
questions.changes: Decides plain files versus a builder-specific format, and what deployment means.
questions.if_skipped: A static site with no server, deployable to any free host, domain handled later.

questions.q: Will most people open this on a phone or a laptop?
questions.changes: Decides which layout is designed first and how heavy pages may be.
questions.if_skipped: Mobile first, and it must also look right on a laptop.

questions.q: Does anything need to be collected or sent: a contact form, sign-ups, payments, bookings?
questions.changes: Adds a backend or a third-party service, plus privacy and spam handling.
questions.if_skipped: A simple contact link by email, with no forms, payments or stored data.

questions.q: Should it be found through search, or will you send people to it directly?
questions.changes: Determines page titles, structure, speed work and whether to write for keywords.
questions.if_skipped: People arrive by direct link, so search work is limited to correct titles and descriptions.

questions.q: Describe one person using it start to finish in a normal session. What do they do, click by click?
questions.changes: Defines the core flow, which is the only part that must be perfect.
questions.if_skipped: A single main screen where the user enters something and sees a result immediately.

questions.q: Where should it run?
questions.changes: Fixes the technology stack and how the user installs or opens it.
questions.if_skipped: A web page that works in any modern browser and on a phone.

questions.q: What information does it keep, and must it still be there tomorrow?
questions.changes: Decides storage: in the browser, a file, or a real database.
questions.if_skipped: Data stays in the user's own browser, with export to a file.

questions.q: Is it for you alone, a small team, or the public, and do people need accounts?
questions.changes: Decides sign-in, permissions, hosting and security effort.
questions.if_skipped: Just the requester, no accounts and no sign-in.

questions.q: What is the worst thing that could go wrong when someone uses it, and how bad is it?
questions.changes: Sets validation, confirmations, undo and backup effort.
questions.if_skipped: Worst case is lost or wrong data, so it confirms before deleting and allows export.

questions.q: Must it connect to a tool you already use, or replace one?
questions.changes: Adds integrations or a migration path and fixes the data format.
questions.if_skipped: It stands alone and imports or exports plain CSV files.

questions.q: How much data or traffic in a year: tens, thousands, or millions of items or users?
questions.changes: Decides whether a simple design is enough or the structure must scale.
questions.if_skipped: Thousands of items at most, so a simple design is fine.

questions.q: If only three features survived, which three?
questions.changes: Produces the must-have list by forced ranking.
questions.if_skipped: The three features are the core flow, saving, and export.

questions.q: Is there a language, framework or hosting you must use, or must avoid?
questions.changes: Prevents building in a stack the user cannot run or maintain.
questions.if_skipped: Plain, widely used technology with no build step where possible.

questions.q: What starts it: a time, an incoming item, a click, or a change somewhere?
questions.changes: Defines the trigger, the first and most fragile step.
questions.if_skipped: It runs on a fixed schedule once a day.

questions.q: Walk me through what you do by hand today, step by step, from the trigger to the last click.
questions.changes: The manual process is the specification. Each step becomes a block or a script.
questions.if_skipped: The manual process is a short linear list of steps with no branches.

questions.q: Which tools does it touch, and can it use their official connections or API keys?
questions.changes: Decides platform (no-code, script or agent) and what access is needed.
questions.if_skipped: It uses only tools the requester already has, through their official connectors.

questions.q: How often will it run and how many items each time?
questions.changes: Sets cost, rate limits and whether it needs batching or queueing.
questions.if_skipped: A few runs a day with under a hundred items each.

questions.q: When it breaks at 3 a.m., who should be told, how, and should it stop or keep going?
questions.changes: Defines error handling, alerts and retry behavior.
questions.if_skipped: It stops, keeps the failed item, and sends one email to the requester.

questions.q: Is there a step where a person must check before it acts on the outside world?
questions.changes: Decides whether it drafts or acts, which is the biggest safety choice.
questions.if_skipped: A person approves anything that leaves the building, such as emails or payments.

questions.q: What if the same item shows up twice, or arrives late or out of order?
questions.changes: Adds duplicate checks and ordering rules.
questions.if_skipped: Items are matched by a unique ID and duplicates are skipped and logged.

questions.q: Who will fix it when a connected tool changes, and how will they find out what it did?
questions.changes: Decides logging, naming and documentation.
questions.if_skipped: It writes a plain log of each run and is described in a short readme.

questions.q: After reading it, what should the reader decide, do or believe?
questions.changes: Sets the structure: lead with the ask and the evidence for it.
questions.if_skipped: The reader should approve or reject one clear recommendation.

questions.q: Who reads it first, and how many minutes will they give it?
questions.changes: Sets length and whether a one-paragraph summary comes first.
questions.if_skipped: The reader is busy and gives it five minutes, so it opens with a short summary.

questions.q: How long should it be, in pages, and is there a template you must follow?
questions.changes: Fixes the length budget and structure up front.
questions.if_skipped: Two to four pages in a plain business layout.

questions.q: Which facts, figures and quotes must appear, and where do they come from?
questions.changes: Prevents invented numbers and lists what must be cited.
questions.if_skipped: Only facts from the material given are used, and each is labeled with its source.

questions.q: Should it sound formal, plain and direct, or persuasive?
questions.changes: Sets voice, sentence length and the use of first person.
questions.if_skipped: Plain and direct, no jargon, short sentences.

questions.q: Does anyone external or legal need to see it, and is anything in it confidential?
questions.changes: Adds review steps, hedged wording and confidentiality marks.
questions.if_skipped: Nothing confidential is included, and it is internal unless told otherwise.

questions.q: What is the strongest objection a skeptical reader will raise?
questions.changes: Adds a section that answers the objection instead of hoping it is not raised.
questions.if_skipped: The main risk and cost objections are answered briefly in their own section.

questions.q: Which sections must it contain, and in what order, if a template or house style applies?
questions.changes: Fixes the outline before writing, so nothing has to be reshuffled later.
questions.if_skipped: A standard outline: summary, background, findings, recommendation, next steps.

questions.q: What do you want the room to do at the end of the last slide?
questions.changes: Defines the closing slide and the narrative direction of the whole deck.
questions.if_skipped: The audience should agree to one clear next step.

questions.q: Who is in the room, how many, and how do they feel about the topic today?
questions.changes: Sets how much to persuade versus explain, and the opening.
questions.if_skipped: A small group of colleagues who are neutral and short of time.

questions.q: How long do you get to speak, and is it presented live or read alone?
questions.changes: Decides slide count, text density and whether notes are needed. A read deck needs more words than a live one.
questions.if_skipped: Presented live for about 15 minutes, roughly one slide per minute.

questions.q: What numbers, quotes, screenshots or images do you already have for it?
questions.changes: Real assets replace filler images and invented charts.
questions.if_skipped: Only the content given is used, and image slots are clearly marked as placeholders.

questions.q: Is there a template or brand kit to follow, and which fonts and colors?
questions.changes: Sets the master layout and theme instead of a made-up design.
questions.if_skipped: A clean, plain theme with one accent color and large type.

questions.q: What question do you dread getting, and what is the honest answer?
questions.changes: Adds a backup or appendix slide for the hardest question.
questions.if_skipped: One appendix slide covers the likely hardest question.

questions.q: Which deck have you seen that impressed you, and what made it work?
questions.changes: Sets pacing and style: minimal and visual versus dense and analytical.
questions.if_skipped: Minimal slides, one idea each, with detail kept for the notes.

questions.q: Do you want speaker notes, a handout, or both?
questions.changes: Adds extra outputs that change how the text is split between slide and page.
questions.if_skipped: Speaker notes are included and there is no handout.

questions.q: What exact decision will the answer feed, and what would you do differently for each possible answer?
questions.changes: Frames the analysis around a decision and drops everything that cannot change it.
questions.if_skipped: The analysis supports one decision, and a clear recommendation is stated up front.

questions.q: Where is the data, how big is it, and how much do you trust it?
questions.changes: Sets the cleaning effort and the strength of the caveats.
questions.if_skipped: The data is one file that is roughly correct but has some missing values.

questions.q: Which time period and which segments matter, and what should be excluded?
questions.changes: Defines filters, comparisons and what counts as an outlier.
questions.if_skipped: The most recent full period, with all segments shown and no exclusions.

questions.q: Who reads the result, and do they want the number, the chart or the reasoning?
questions.changes: Sets the level of detail and the format of the deliverable.
questions.if_skipped: Answer first, then charts, then a short methods note.

questions.q: What do you already believe the answer is, and what would surprise you?
questions.changes: Reveals bias to test against and what would count as a real finding.
questions.if_skipped: The expected result is unknown, and any result is reported even if it is unexpected.

questions.q: Are there business definitions I must use, such as what counts as an active customer?
questions.changes: Wrong definitions silently change every number, so they are fixed up front.
questions.if_skipped: Standard definitions are used and each one is written out in the report.

questions.q: Is any of the data personal or confidential, and where may it be processed?
questions.changes: Decides whether data must stay local and whether identifiers are stripped.
questions.if_skipped: The data is treated as confidential and never leaves the local machine.

questions.q: Is this a one-time answer or something you will rerun next month?
questions.changes: Decides whether to deliver a reusable script or just the result.
questions.if_skipped: A one-time answer, with the steps written down so it could be repeated.

questions.q: What question should the sheet answer at a glance when you open it?
questions.changes: Defines the summary view that the whole layout supports.
questions.if_skipped: One summary tab shows the key totals and a check that inputs are complete.

questions.q: What goes in by hand, what is pasted from elsewhere, and what must be calculated?
questions.changes: Separates inputs, data and formulas, which is the core structure of a reliable model.
questions.if_skipped: Inputs are on one tab and clearly colored, and everything else is calculated.

questions.q: Excel, Google Sheets or something else, and which version?
questions.changes: Some functions and features exist in only one tool.
questions.if_skipped: Uses only functions available in both Excel and Google Sheets.

questions.q: Who else fills it in, and how careful are they?
questions.changes: Decides protection, validation lists and instructions on the sheet.
questions.if_skipped: Others may edit it, so inputs are validated and formulas are locked.

questions.q: Which formulas, rates or rules must be exactly right, and where is the source?
questions.changes: Fixes the logic and gives a test case to check the model against.
questions.if_skipped: Rules come from the stated source, and one worked example is included as a check.

questions.q: How many rows will it hold in a year, and will it grow?
questions.changes: Decides whether ranges expand automatically or a database is a better tool.
questions.if_skipped: Under a few thousand rows, using ranges that grow with the data.

questions.q: What is the costliest mistake a wrong number in this sheet could cause?
questions.changes: Sets how many checks and totals-must-match tests to add.
questions.if_skipped: Checks flag any total that does not reconcile.

questions.q: Should it look plain and dense, or polished enough to show to a client?
questions.changes: Sets formatting effort and whether charts and print layout matter.
questions.if_skipped: Clean and readable but not designed for clients.

questions.q: What single number should move, by how much, and by when?
questions.changes: Picks the one metric that every asset and channel is judged against.
questions.if_skipped: One number is chosen: sign-ups or sales, with a target set after the first week of data.

questions.q: What exactly are you offering, at what price, and why should anyone act now?
questions.changes: The offer and its deadline drive every message; weak offers cannot be fixed by copy.
questions.if_skipped: The offer is the existing product at its current price, with no artificial deadline.

questions.q: Describe the one person you most want to reach, and where they spend time online.
questions.changes: Selects channels and the language of the copy.
questions.if_skipped: The target is the existing best customer type, reached where the brand already posts.

questions.q: What is the budget in money and in hours, and who does the work?
questions.changes: Decides paid versus organic and how many assets are realistic.
questions.if_skipped: Almost no paid budget, and the work is done by the requester alone.

questions.q: What do you already have: audience list, past results, testimonials, images?
questions.changes: Reuses proven material instead of starting cold.
questions.if_skipped: Only material named in the conversation is used, with no invented testimonials.

questions.q: What was the last campaign, what did it get, and what would you change?
questions.changes: Past results are the best forecast and show what to avoid repeating.
questions.if_skipped: There is no history, so the plan includes a small test before scaling.

questions.q: Are there claims you cannot make, or platform and legal rules that apply?
questions.changes: Prevents ads that get rejected or create legal exposure.
questions.if_skipped: No guarantees, no unproven numbers, and no medical or financial promises.

questions.q: What happens to someone who says yes: who follows up and how fast?
questions.changes: A campaign that outruns its follow-up wastes the leads; this sets the handoff.
questions.if_skipped: The requester follows up personally within one day.

questions.q: What is the one idea a reader should remember, in a single sentence?
questions.changes: Sets the thesis; everything that does not serve it is cut.
questions.if_skipped: The single idea is the one already stated in the request.

questions.q: Who is the reader, and what do they think about this topic right now?
questions.changes: Decides the starting point and how much persuasion versus explanation is needed.
questions.if_skipped: The reader is intelligent but new to the topic.

questions.q: Where will it be published, and what are the length and format limits there?
questions.changes: Platform rules decide length, structure and how the opening works.
questions.if_skipped: A standalone piece of about 800 words, posted on the requester's own channel.

questions.q: Send two things you wrote that sound like you. What do you never say?
questions.changes: Real writing samples give the voice; the never list removes AI-sounding habits.
questions.if_skipped: A plain, direct voice with short sentences and no buzzwords.

questions.q: What real stories, numbers or examples from your own experience belong in it?
questions.changes: Personal proof separates the piece from generic content.
questions.if_skipped: Only examples provided are used, and any missing example is flagged, not invented.

questions.q: What should the reader do after the last line?
questions.changes: Defines the ending and what is measured afterwards.
questions.if_skipped: The ending invites a reply or a follow, with no hard sell.

questions.q: What is the take that others in this space are not saying, or that you disagree with?
questions.changes: Provides the angle that makes the piece worth reading.
questions.if_skipped: A clear, practical point of view is taken, with one honest caveat.

questions.q: Is this a one-off or the first of a series in the same style?
questions.changes: A series needs a repeatable format and consistent structure.
questions.if_skipped: A one-off piece.

questions.q: What single reply or action do you want from this email?
questions.changes: One clear ask decides the subject line, the ending and the length.
questions.if_skipped: The ask is a short reply saying yes or no.

questions.q: Who receives it, what is your relationship, and what do they know about you?
questions.changes: Sets tone, formality and how much context the email must carry.
questions.if_skipped: The recipient does not know the sender well, so the tone is polite and brief.

questions.q: What happened before, and what facts must be mentioned exactly?
questions.changes: Prevents wrong references to earlier messages, dates and figures.
questions.if_skipped: Only facts from the thread or notes are used, with nothing assumed.

questions.q: Warm, neutral or firm, and can you paste an email of yours that sounds right?
questions.changes: Sets the voice; a real sample is better than the adjective.
questions.if_skipped: Neutral and friendly, with no exclamation marks.

questions.q: Is anything here delicate: money, a complaint, a refusal, a legal matter?
questions.changes: Delicate emails need softer framing and often a review before sending.
questions.if_skipped: Nothing is delicate, and no threats or promises are made.

questions.q: One email or a sequence, and how many days between messages?
questions.changes: Sequences need a plan for each message and a stop rule.
questions.if_skipped: One email, with an optional short follow-up.

questions.q: How long can it be: two lines or a full page?
questions.changes: Sets density and what gets cut.
questions.if_skipped: Under 120 words.

questions.q: Do you send it yourself, or should I only draft it for you to review?
questions.changes: Drafting keeps the human check on anything sent in the user's name.
questions.if_skipped: Drafts only. Nothing is sent without explicit approval.

questions.q: What does the finished plan look like at the end, in concrete terms?
questions.changes: Defines the finish line that the plan works backward from.
questions.if_skipped: The end state is the one stated in the request, with a clear date.

questions.q: Where are you starting from: what exists today, what resources do you have?
questions.changes: A plan from the wrong starting point is fiction; this fixes the baseline.
questions.if_skipped: The starting point is close to zero with normal working hours available.

questions.q: How many hours a week can you really give it, and what fixed dates are there?
questions.changes: Sets the real pace of the plan and the milestones that cannot slide.
questions.if_skipped: Five hours a week, no fixed dates other than the final one.

questions.q: What is the budget, and what may be spent without asking?
questions.changes: Separates free options from paid ones.
questions.if_skipped: Low budget, and any purchase is flagged for approval.

questions.q: What has derailed a plan like this before?
questions.changes: Builds the known failure into the plan as a risk with a countermeasure.
questions.if_skipped: The usual risks are time slips and lost motivation, so each phase has a small first step.

questions.q: Who else is involved, and who decides when the plan changes?
questions.changes: Assigns owners and decision rights.
questions.if_skipped: The requester owns and decides everything.

questions.q: Do you want a one-page outline, a week-by-week schedule, or a checklist?
questions.changes: Sets the level of detail and how the result is used day to day.
questions.if_skipped: A one-page outline plus a week-by-week table.

questions.q: How and when will you check whether the plan is working and change it?
questions.changes: Adds review dates and the rule that triggers a change.
questions.if_skipped: A review every two weeks, with a stated trigger for changing course.

questions.q: What starts this process, and what marks it as finished?
questions.changes: Defines the start and end, which are the borders of the whole document.
questions.if_skipped: The process starts with a request and ends with a confirmed result.

questions.q: Who will follow it, how experienced are they, and will they read it or need it in the moment?
questions.changes: Decides checklist versus narrative and how much explanation each step needs.
questions.if_skipped: New team members follow it step by step while doing the work.

questions.q: Walk me through how it is really done today, including the shortcuts.
questions.changes: The real process differs from the official one; the document must match reality.
questions.if_skipped: The steps described in the request are the real process.

questions.q: What are the three most common exceptions, and what should someone do?
questions.changes: Exceptions are where processes fail, so they get their own branches.
questions.if_skipped: Exceptions are escalated to the process owner.

questions.q: Who owns it, and who signs off on changes?
questions.changes: Names the owner and the change rule, which keeps the document alive.
questions.if_skipped: The requester owns it and can change it at any time.

questions.q: Which tools and accounts are involved, and can everyone access them?
questions.changes: Steps must name real tools and permissions, not generic ones.
questions.if_skipped: Only tools named in the request are used, and access is assumed.

questions.q: How will you know the process was followed correctly?
questions.changes: Adds checkpoints and a way to verify each stage.
questions.if_skipped: A short checklist at the end confirms each key step.

questions.q: Where will people open it while working: wiki page, shared folder, or a printed sheet at the desk?
questions.changes: Sets layout for where it will actually be read.
questions.if_skipped: A single document that prints on one or two pages.

questions.q: What exactly do you want to find out, and what decision depends on it?
questions.changes: A sharp question sets the scope; a decision sets what evidence is enough.
questions.if_skipped: The question is the one in the request, tied to a single decision.

questions.q: How deep: a quick scan in an hour, or a careful review you would defend in a meeting?
questions.changes: Sets the number of sources and how strictly claims are checked.
questions.if_skipped: A solid summary with sources listed for each claim.

questions.q: Which sources do you trust or distrust, and are there ones I must include?
questions.changes: Fixes the evidence base and avoids sources the reader will reject.
questions.if_skipped: Primary and reputable sources are preferred, and each claim is cited.

questions.q: What do you already know or suspect? Which parts are settled?
questions.changes: Avoids repeating known ground and shows what to test rather than confirm.
questions.if_skipped: Nothing is treated as settled, and the findings are checked from scratch.

questions.q: Who reads the result, and do they want a verdict, options, or raw findings?
questions.changes: Decides the deliverable form and how firm the conclusions should be.
questions.if_skipped: A short verdict up front, then the evidence.

questions.q: What time window and geography count as current or relevant?
questions.changes: Old or foreign sources may be irrelevant; this sets the cutoff.
questions.if_skipped: Sources from the last two years, worldwide, with dates shown.

questions.q: How should I show what is uncertain or disputed?
questions.changes: Decides how gaps and disagreement between sources are reported.
questions.if_skipped: Uncertain claims are flagged inline with the reason.

questions.q: How should evidence be shown: inline links, footnotes, or a table of claim against source?
questions.changes: Sets how easily the reader can verify each finding.
questions.if_skipped: A table of claim, source and date next to each finding.
